input: Investigate remote volunteer opportunities for digital skills

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Digital skills is a broad term — knowing whether the user means coding, data analysis, social media, graphic design, cybersecurity, etc. will completely change which opportunities are relevant.
The beneficiary type (nonprofits, schools, elderly individuals, developing communities, etc.) affects which platforms and organisations to target.
How many hours per week or month the user can commit determines whether to look for micro-volunteering, project-based, or ongoing roles.
Whether the user is looking to start immediately or at a future date, and any geographic or time-zone constraints, affects which opportunities are practically accessible.
Whether the user wants to teach/train others vs. build something (e.g., a website or database) vs. consult will shape the type of role to seek.
Knowing what the user wants to get out of this — career development, personal fulfilment, networking, building a portfolio — determines how to prioritise and evaluate opportunities.
Whether the user wants a curated shortlist, a step-by-step action plan, or help with a profile/application affects the immediate next deliverable.

gold.taskTitle: Find Remote Volunteering Opportunities in Digital Skills
gold.taskDescription: Research and identify remote volunteer opportunities where the user can contribute their digital skills to a cause or organisation.

questions.title: Which specific digital skills do you want to volunteer?
questions.description: Identify the exact skill area(s) the user wants to contribute — e.g., web development, data analysis, social media management, graphic design, cybersecurity, digital literacy training.

questions.title: What type of cause or beneficiary matters most to you?
questions.description: Determine the kind of organisation or community the user wants to support — e.g., nonprofits, schools, small businesses, underserved communities, environmental groups.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you realistically commit?
questions.description: Understand the user's availability to filter for micro-volunteering, short-term projects, or ongoing part-time roles.

questions.title: When are you looking to start volunteering?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants to begin immediately or is planning ahead, which affects urgency and the type of opportunities to prioritise.

questions.title: Do you prefer teaching others or building something hands-on?
questions.description: Distinguish between roles focused on training/mentoring others in digital skills versus roles where the user directly builds tools, content, or systems.

questions.title: What do you most want to gain from this experience?
questions.description: Identify the user's primary motivation — e.g., portfolio building, career transition, personal fulfilment, networking, or giving back — to prioritise the best-fit opportunities.

questions.title: What output would help you most right now?
questions.description: Determine the immediate deliverable the user needs — a curated list of platforms, a step-by-step action plan, help crafting a volunteer profile, or something else.
